2. The facts are that Mr. Latifur Rahman, acting as Upazila Nirbahi Officer, Kalinakanda Upazila wrote Memo No. 41 dated 17.1.1985 to the Upazila. Magistrate, Kalmakanda to the eject that out of a total lifted wheat of 1168 maunds accused petitioner Abdul Mannan in his capacity as a public servant, i.e. Chairman, No. 8 Rongchhati Union Parishad, Kalmakanda dishonestly misappropriated 484 mds of wheat which was meant for distribution amongst distressed women (Vulnerable Group Feeding) The case for the defence is that the accused petitioner had distributed the total amount of lifted wheat among distressed women as per Master Rolls submitted to the District Magistrate. Neither the police nor the Bureau of Anti-Corruption investigated into the case apparently because no complaint was sent to them and so the police or the bureau of Anti-Corruption has submitted no charge-sheet ( i e. a report in writing) in this case. It is provided in sub-section 1 of section 5 of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 as follows : ''5(1) Notwithstanding anything contained in the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, or in any other law, the offence specified in the schedule shall be triable exclusively by a Special Judge". 

 3. The alleged offence comes within the ambit of section 409 of the Penal Code which is included in the said schedule of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958. Instead of sending the complaint to the Senior Special Judge or to the District Anti-corruption Officer complainant U.N.O. Mr. Latifur Rahman himself acting as Upazila Magistrate, Kalma-kanda took cognizance of the case and issued warrant of arrest against the accused petitioner Abdul Manama, Chairman, Ranchhari Union Parishad on 17.1.85 stating that he had perused his own petition of complaint and examined two witnesses and that there is a prima fade case against the said accused petitioner under section 409 of the Penal Code. In view of the above quoted provision of section 5(1) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 the Upazila Magistrate, Kalmakanda has no jurisdiction to take cognizance of the said offence under section 401) of the Penal Code against the accused petitioner (a public servant) and to issue warrant of arrest against him. In view of the fact that in addition to the provision of the above quoted section 4(1) and section 5(1) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 a Special Judge alone is competent to take cognizance of any offence committed within his jurisdiction triable under the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 upon receiving a complaint of facts which constitute such offence or upon report in writing of such acts made by any police officer. The said order dated 17.1.85 passed by Mr. Latifur Rahman acting as upazila Magistrate being without jurisdiction is liable to be set aside in exercise of our power tattier section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. It may be stated that the District Magistrate, Netrokona has referred the case to this Court for quashing the proceedings against accused petitioner apparently in exercise of our power under section 561 of the Cr.P.C., but we do not do so as it cannot be said in this case that complaint does not disclose any prima facie case although it is true that there was no enquiry worth the name and the accused was given no opportunity whatsoever to explain the matter. But on the grounds stated above the proceedings in question in the Court of Upazila Magistrate, Kalmakanda against the accused petitioner cannot continue as we are setting aside the initial order of cognizance and ,issuance of process against the accused petitioner passed on 17.1.85. 

 4. In the result, the order dated 17.1.85 passed by the Upazila Magistrate, Kalma-kanda, District Netrokona in C.R. Case No. 1(3) 85 taking cognizance of the offence under section 400 of the Penal Code and issuing warrant of arrest against the accused petitioner Abdul Mannan, Chairman, Rangchhati Union Parishad is set aside in exercise of our power under section 439 Cr P.C. We direct that the proceedings in question in the court of the Upazila Magistrate, Kalmakands shall not continue in view of the aforesaid provisions of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958. The reference is disposed of in the above terms; -
